---
title: "Stock assessments"
---

How many of the stocks ICES gives advice on have their assessment in TAF, and how far along it is.

Each stock is placed by the [TAF readiness level](../system/readiness-level.qmd) of its assessment repository in [ices-taf](https://github.com/ices-taf) for the year. A stock is published when it also has a repository for the year in [ices-advice](https://github.com/ices-advice). The stocks, their expert group and data category come from the [ICES Stock Database](https://sd.ices.dk). The individual assessments are listed under [TAF readiness](readiness.qmd).

```{r}
#| include: false
source("_plot.R")

stocks <- read.csv("../_generated/stocks.csv")
stocks$category <- factor(stocks$category, c("Category 1", "Categories 2-6"))

# from the most to the least advanced, the order the bars are stacked in
states <- c("Level 2", "Level 1", "No level", "No repository")
state_colours <- setNames(c("#3987e5", "#9ec5f4", "#c9c8c1", "#efeeea"), states)
stocks$state <- factor(
  ifelse(is.na(stocks$level), "No repository", ifelse(stocks$level == 0, "No level", paste("Level", stocks$level))),
  states
)
# in TAF to some degree: there is code, so level 1 or above
stocks$in_taf <- stocks$level %in% 1:4

latest <- stocks[stocks$year == max(stocks$year), ]
percent <- function(x) sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * mean(x))
```

In `r max(stocks$year)`, `r sum(latest$in_taf)` of the `r nrow(latest)` stocks (`r percent(latest$in_taf)`) have assessment code in TAF, at level 1 or above, and `r sum(latest$level %in% 2)` of them have reached level 2. Another `r sum(latest$level %in% 0)` stocks have a repository with no code in it yet. `r sum(latest$published)` stocks are published.

## Stocks by readiness level

Each year has two bars: one for the category 1 stocks and one for the stocks in categories 2 to 6. The height of a bar is the number of stocks, and the lines show how many of them are published.

```{r}
#| echo: false
counts <- as.data.frame(table(year = stocks$year, category = stocks$category, state = stocks$state))
counts <- counts[order(counts$year, counts$category), ]
published <- aggregate(published ~ year + category, stocks, sum)
published <- published[order(published$year, published$category), ]
# nothing was published before the first year with a published stock
published <- published[published$year >= min(c(published$year[published$published > 0], Inf)), ]

# two bars a year: the x axis is the year and, within it, the category
short <- c("Category 1" = "1", "Categories 2-6" = "2-6")
bar_x <- function(d) list(as.character(d$year), unname(short[as.character(d$category)]))

p <- plot_ly()
for (state in states) {
  d <- counts[counts$state == state, ]
  p <- p |>
    add_bars(
      x = bar_x(d), y = d$Freq, name = state,
      marker = list(color = state_colours[[state]], line = list(color = "white", width = 2)),
      customdata = paste(d$category, d$year),
      hovertemplate = "%{customdata}: %{y} stocks"
    )
}
for (category in levels(stocks$category)) {
  d <- published[published$category == category, ]
  p <- p |>
    add_trace(
      x = bar_x(d), y = d$published, name = paste("Published,", tolower(category)),
      type = "scatter", mode = "lines+markers",
      line = list(color = orange, width = 2, dash = if (category == "Category 1") "solid" else "dot"),
      marker = list(color = orange, size = 8, line = list(color = "white", width = 2)),
      customdata = paste(d$category, d$year),
      hovertemplate = "%{customdata}: %{y} published"
    )
}
p |>
  taf_layout(
    barmode = "stack",
    xaxis = list(title = "Data category, by year"),
    yaxis = list(title = "Stocks")
  ) |>
  layout(legend = list(traceorder = "normal"))
```

## Coverage by expert group

The percentage of each expert group's stocks that have assessment code in TAF, at level 1 or above. Click a group in the legend to hide it, and double-click to show it on its own.

```{r}
#| echo: false
groups <- aggregate(cbind(in_taf, level2 = level %in% 2, published, stocks = 1) ~ eg + year, stocks, sum)
groups$coverage <- 100 * groups$in_taf / groups$stocks

# the league table: the groups in the latest year, most covered first
league <- groups[groups$year == max(groups$year), ]
league <- league[order(-league$coverage, -league$in_taf, league$eg), ]

# eight colours, then the same again with dashed and dotted lines
palette <- c("#2a78d6", "#eb6834", "#1baf7a", "#eda100", "#e87ba4", "#008300", "#6250d6", "#e34948")
dashes <- c("solid", "dash", "dot")

p <- plot_ly()
for (i in seq_len(nrow(league))) {
  d <- groups[groups$eg == league$eg[i], ]
  colour <- palette[(i - 1) %% length(palette) + 1]
  p <- p |>
    add_trace(
      data = d, x = ~year, y = ~coverage, name = league$eg[i],
      type = "scatter", mode = "lines+markers",
      line = list(color = colour, width = 2, dash = dashes[(i - 1) %/% length(palette) + 1]),
      marker = list(color = colour, size = 6),
      customdata = ~paste(in_taf, "of", stocks),
      hovertemplate = "%{x}: %{y:.0f}% (%{customdata} stocks)"
    )
}
p |>
  taf_layout(
    xaxis = list(title = "", dtick = 1),
    yaxis = list(title = "Stocks with code in TAF", ticksuffix = "%", range = c(-3, 103))
  ) |>
  layout(legend = list(orientation = "v", x = 1.02, y = 1))
```

The groups in `r max(stocks$year)`, ordered by coverage.

```{r}
#| echo: false
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    "Expert group" = league$eg,
    "Stocks" = league$stocks,
    "With code in TAF" = league$in_taf,
    "Coverage" = sprintf("%.0f%%", league$coverage),
    "Level 2" = league$level2,
    "Published" = league$published,
    check.names = FALSE
  ),
  row.names = FALSE, align = "lrrrrr"
)
```
